syllabus_topics: Singular and plural subjects with matching verbs
Ignoring prepositional phrases between subject and verb
Indefinite pronouns: each, everyone, somebody, nobody (singular)
Compound subjects with 'and' (plural); 'or/nor' agrees with the nearer subject
Collective nouns (team, committee, jury) take singular verbs
Amounts and measurements (ten dollars, news, mathematics) take singular verbs
skills.title: Subject-verb agreement

syllabus_topics: Present, past, and future tense consistency within a sentence
Time markers (yesterday, since 2019, currently) governing tense choice
No inappropriate shifts between past and present
skills.title: Verb tense and consistency

syllabus_topics: Ambiguous or vague pronouns with no clear antecedent
skills.title: Pronoun clarity and agreement

syllabus_topics: Identifying the central idea of a short passage
Distinguishing main idea from supporting detail
Summarizing what a text is mostly about
skills.title: Main idea and central details

syllabus_topics: Drawing logical conclusions from stated information
Command of textual evidence: citing lines that support an answer
Distinguishing supported inference from unsupported speculation
skills.title: Inference and textual evidence

source: College Board digital SAT Reading and Writing content domains (satsuite.collegeboard.org): Craft and Structure (~13-15 questions); Information and Ideas (~12-14); Standard English Conventions (~11-15, including subject-verb agreement, verb forms and tenses, pronouns and pronoun-antecedent agreement, punctuation); Expression of Ideas (~8-12). Grammar skills mapped to Standard English Conventions; main-idea and inference mapped to Information and Ideas. Sequencing: L1 Foundation → L2 Intermediate → L3 Advanced → L4 Exam mastery (beginner to advanced).
title: Reading & Writing: Conventions and Ideas
